traceability.evidence: Story file docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md defines acceptance criteria and requirements REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE, REQ-ESLINT-COMPAT, REQ-RULE-REGISTRY, REQ-CONFIG-SYSTEM, REQ-NPM-PACKAGE, REQ-TYPESCRIPT, REQ-TEST-SETUP, REQ-ERROR-HANDLING. All are referenced by implementation and tests.,Core plugin implementation in src/index.ts: - Exports a plugin object with { rules, configs, maintenance, meta } (default export) and named exports { rules, configs, maintenance }. - RULE_NAMES array lists core rules: require-story-annotation, require-req-annotation, require-branch-annotation, valid-annotation-format, valid-story-reference, valid-req-reference, prefer-implements-annotation, require-test-traceability, satisfying REQ-RULE-REGISTRY. - Dynamically requires ./rules/${name} in a try/catch and falls back to a placeholder RuleModule while logging to console.error if loading fails, satisfying REQ-ERROR-HANDLING. - pluginMeta function reads name/version from ../../package.json or ../package.json with a safe fallback, and returns { name, version, namespace: 'traceability' }, satisfying REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE and REQ-NPM-PACKAGE. - TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES and createTraceabilityFlatConfig() construct flat-config fragments; configs.recommended and configs.strict are arrays of flat config objects using those severities, satisfying REQ-CONFIG-SYSTEM and contributing to REQ-ESLINT-COMPAT. - Maintenance API (detectStaleAnnotations, updateAnnotationReferences, batchUpdateAnnotations, verifyAnnotations, generateMaintenanceReport) is exported under plugin.maintenance, matching the documented architecture.,Tests specifically for plugin structure and meta (Core Functionality, Quality Standards, Rule Registry, Config System): - tests/plugin-setup.test.ts (tagged with @story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md): - "[REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE] plugin exports rules and configs" asserts rules/configs exist, are objects, and match plugin.rules/plugin.configs. - "[REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE][REQ-NPM-PACKAGE] plugin exposes meta with name, namespace, and version" reads package.json and asserts plugin.meta.name/version/namespace. - tests/plugin-default-export-and-configs.test.ts (also supporting this story): - Verifies default export includes rules and configs. - Asserts rules object keys are in expected insertion order, including prefer-supports-annotation alias, validating REQ-RULE-REGISTRY. - Asserts configs.recommended[0].rules maps core rules to 'error' and valid-annotation-format to 'warn', and configs.strict[0].rules equals configs.recommended[0].rules, satisfying REQ-CONFIG-SYSTEM and error severity mapping. - These tests are referenced directly in the story acceptance criteria for "Core Functionality" and "Quality Standards" and passed in the latest test run.,ESLint v9 flat-config integration (REQ-ESLINT-COMPAT / Integration acceptance criterion): - tests/config/flat-config-presets-integration.test.ts uses FlatESLint from 'eslint/use-at-your-own-risk', builds flat overrideConfig as [baseConfig, ...configs.recommended] and [baseConfig, ...configs.strict], and lints simple functions. - Both tests assert that the resulting lint messages include 'traceability/require-story-annotation', proving that the exported configs.recommended and configs.strict integrate correctly with ESLint v9 flat config. - README.md and user-docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md provide concrete ESLint v9 flat config examples that match this usage: - README: example eslint.config.js importing traceability and spreading ...traceability.configs.recommended. - user-docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md: multiple flat-config examples (JS-only, TS, mixed, monorepo) all use plugins: { traceability } and ...traceability.configs.recommended or ...traceability.configs.strict.,User experience & installation/config docs (User Experience acceptance criterion): - README.md includes: - Installation instructions with npm/yarn for eslint-plugin-traceability. - Clear flat-config usage examples for ESLint v9, showing how to register the plugin and apply recommended/strict presets. - Quick Start example annotating a function with @story/@req. - Commands for running ESLint with the plugin to validate missing @story annotations, as well as testing and quality check scripts. - user-docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md provides a detailed ESLint 9 flat config guide including Quick Setup, Common Configuration Patterns, TypeScript integration, troubleshooting, and a working example for a TypeScript plugin project, all demonstrating how to use this plugin in real projects.,Error handling behavior (REQ-ERROR-HANDLING acceptance criterion): - src/index.ts loads each rule in a try/catch and on failure: - Logs `[eslint-plugin-traceability] Failed to load rule "${name}": ${error.message}` to console.error. - Registers a placeholder rule whose meta.docs.description indicates load failure and whose create() reports an error on Program. - tests/plugin-setup-error.test.ts: - Uses jest.mock to make '../src/rules/require-branch-annotation' throw an Error("Test load error"). - Requires '../src/index' and asserts console.error was called with a message containing 'Failed to load rule "require-branch-annotation": Test load error'. - Asserts a placeholderRule exists in plugin.rules["require-branch-annotation"] and that calling its create() visitor reports a message containing 'Error loading rule "require-branch-annotation": Test load error'. - tests/cli-error-handling.test.ts: - Spawns the ESLint CLI with this plugin and configuration via a real eslint CLI binary, using stdin. - Expects non-zero exit status and checks that stdout contains the specific, user-friendly message for missing @story annotations, demonstrating that CLI-level error handling and messaging are surfaced correctly when rules are enforced. - Both test files are tagged with @story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md and @req REQ-ERROR-HANDLING, directly confirming this requirement.,Documentation for plugin structure and development setup (Documentation acceptance criterion): - traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria for 001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP are fully implemented and verified. The plugin exposes a standards-compliant ESLint plugin object with metadata, rule registry, and flat-config presets; integrates correctly with ESLint v9 flat config; includes clear installation and configuration documentation; and implements robust error handling for rule loading both at module and CLI level. The project is written in TypeScript with a comprehensive Jest-based test suite, and all referenced tests for this story pass in the latest run. Therefore, this story is considered PASSED.
